title: Blizzard Spent 7 Years on WoW's Successor, Then Cancelled It
hook: Blizzard spent seven years and about 140 developers on Titan, the planned successor to WoW, then scrapped it in 2014 and gave the survivors six weeks to pitch something new. That pitch became Overwatch. Which cancelled game do you wish had survived?
script: Did you know Blizzard spent seven years building a follow up to World of Warcraft, then threw the whole thing away? The project was called Titan. Work on it began around two thousand seven, only three years after WoW launched. It was meant to be Blizzard's next giant online game, a massively multiplayer shooter instead of a fantasy RPG. At its peak the Titan team had grown to about one hundred forty artists, designers and engineers. Then in the spring of two thousand thirteen Blizzard tore up the version it had. Most of the developers were moved to other games. In two thousand fourteen, company president Mike Morhaime confirmed Titan was gone for good. His explanation was simple. We didn't find the fun. We didn't find the passion. Jeff Kaplan, who would go on to direct Overwatch, later said the project failed horrifically in every way. But the small group left behind was given six weeks to pitch something new. They sketched three ideas, two weeks each. One of those pitches was a hero shooter. It became Overwatch, and it launched in May two thousand sixteen, less than two years after Titan's cancellation went public. So WoW's cancelled successor still handed Blizzard its next big hit. Which cancelled game do you wish had survived? Follow for more gaming history.
